text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.

-- Credit Lyonnais posts 67 million francs profits for the first half, prepares for privatisation, for which a state recapitalisation estimated at around eight or nine billion francs is needed. The bank set a 1.5 billion franc provision for restructuring plans. (Les Echos, La Tribune, Le Figaro, Liberation).
LES ECHOS
-- Pharmaceutical firm SmithKline Beecham to cut price of leading antibiotic to resist promotion of cheaper generic drugs, holds prices of new products to finance research.
-- Doctors to join civil servants for October 17 strike.
-- P&O and Stena Line to merge to resist Eurotunnel and reconquer Channel-crossing market, plan job cuts.
-- Family-owned retail group Promodes chairman Paul-Louis Halley seeks French partner for his group, does not rule out bringing the family's stake to under 50 percent.
LA TRIBUNE DESFOSSES
-- President Jacques Chirac says government to study a reform of legislation on buyouts to protect firms from hostile takeovers.
-- State secretary for research Francois d'Aubert wants tax laws to allow savings to be invested in research, as budget austerity limits state financing.
LE FIGARO-ECONOMIE
-- Banques Populaires considers buying Paribas subsidiary Credit du Nord.
LIBERATION (Economic section)
-- IMF Managing Director Michel Camdessus wants IMF to act for better health insurance and labour conditions worldwide, fight corruption and money laundering, to help sustain economic growth.
-- Doctors unions to protest health budget austerity on October 17.
-- Transport minister Bernard Pons says TGV high-speed train project for eastern France remains a priority, even if European train programmes may be scaled down.
-- Jacadi children's clothing group may file for bankruptcy in the next few days.
THE INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE
-- Olivetti to sell personal computer business.
